en.askTitle: Plug in your own shifts, savings and goals and get a data-career plan built from real job ads
en.runTitle: Toronto retail manager to data analyst: 12 hours a week, CAD 6,000, start January 2027

fields.label: Work shifts and weekly study hours
fields.value: Full-time retail store manager; about 12 hours a week for study

fields.label: Education
fields.placeholder: e.g. a business diploma, no degree in a related field

fields.label: Computer and software access
fields.placeholder: e.g. own laptop, Excel at home, no paid BI licence

fields.label: Current pay and minimum acceptable offer

en.template: Help me plan a Toronto retail-to-data transition around {hours}, {education}, {computer}, {pay} and {budget}. Prioritize retail reporting, SQL and one BI tool. Fit projects and applications inside my available hours, flag degree/student restrictions and unconfirmed costs, and keep funding out of the budget until approved. Ask before enrolling, paying, contacting anyone, applying for jobs or sharing employer data.

phases.title: Gather current Toronto job ads, training options and funding rules from public sources
phases.note: Job ads, college and bootcamp pages, Ontario and federal funding rules
phases.judgment: It reported shortfalls instead of padding the list: the second ad researcher verified five current ads rather than twelve, and none was an ordinary junior opening. It also corrected a likely misreading of the Canada Training Credit, which refunds up to half of eligible fees, not an automatic CAD 5,000.

phases.title: Build the sourced job-ad table and a realistic nine-month plan with the calculations
phases.note: Job-ad table, skills summary, training comparison, nine-month plan
phases.judgment: The final write-up says plainly that it did not reach the 25 junior ads asked for. Of the 25 ads it screened, seven were non-student early-career roles and eleven were student-only, and the skills summary uses only those seven.

phases.title: Check the page at desktop and phone widths and deliver the files

workers: Searched public postings for junior Toronto data analyst ads at employers A to L and recorded the skills, experience and pay each one asks for
Did the same for employers M to Z, keeping only ads that could be opened and checked
Checked the official Ontario and federal rules on pay posting, the training credit, Better Jobs Ontario and part-time student aid
Compared college certificate and bootcamp fees, formats, workload and start dates
